heroSub: 8 good-value budget stays in Lopburi we've reviewed in depth — hand-picked for real value, all scoring 7.9+. From a wooden old-town guesthouse you can walk to the monkeys and train station from ฿350/night, to the highest-scoring clean budget chain, to roomy new-town hotels with free parking. From roughly ฿350–700/night.
introH2: 🏯 Can you really do Lopburi on a budget — and which area gives the best value?
introHtml: Lopburi is a town you can genuinely do on a budget, because most stays run from a few hundred to just over a thousand baht, and the main sights — Phra Prang Sam Yot, San Phra Kan, King Narai's Palace, and the famous monkeys — cluster in a walkable old town · the key to keeping costs down is to match your area to how you're travelling — if you arrive by train and want to walk among the monkeys and temples, the old town (Tha Hin–Pa Tan) is the answer, since you can walk to the train station and the sights without a car, and most stays there are budget guesthouses and small resorts · if you self-drive, the new town (Tha Sala–Khao Sam Yot) near Big C and restaurants has free parking and roomier rooms, but it's a ~10-minute drive into the old town for the monkeys · this guide hand-picks 8 Lopburi budget stays we've already reviewed — only the genuinely good-value ones, all scoring 7.9+ — ranked by value, each drawn from real guest-review voices with honest pros and cons, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Lopburi has no metro; getting around relies on cars, except in the old town where you can sightsee on foot · stays in the old town (Tha Hin–Pa Tan) are often walking distance to the train station, Phra Prang Sam Yot, and the monkeys — great for train arrivals without a car, though parking is limited (Noom, Windsor) · new-town (Tha Sala–Khao Sam Yot) stays focus on roomy rooms, free parking, and being near Big C and restaurants, ideal for self-drivers, but it's a ~10-minute drive into the old town to see the monkeys (HOP INN, Charlotte, JRD, Benjatara, Phetlada, Grand) · from Lopburi train station you can walk straight into the old town; if you're driving, book a stay with free parking, which nearly all in this guide have.

entries.addr: 15-17 Phraya Kamjat Rd, Tha Hin, Mueang Lopburi
entries.storyHtml: The best value in this guide, from just ฿350 yet scoring 8.2 from 270 reviews — Noom Guesthouse is a two-storey wooden house in the heart of the old town (Tha Hin), an easy walk to the train station, Phra Prang Sam Yot, and the monkeys with no car needed, which saves on transport too. Real guest reviews praise the tasty, cheap on-site restaurant, the friendly owner, motorbike/bike rental, and the wooden-house character. The trade-offs to be clear about: the cheapest rooms are small and basic with thin walls that carry sound, some are fan-only, and there's no pool or large parking. Best for train arrivals who explore the old town on foot and want an affordable stay with character.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Arriving by train is the best value — walk over from Lopburi station with no extra fare. For A/C and an en-suite, ask for an A/C Double/Twin; the fan rooms are cheaper but basic. Try the on-site restaurant many reviews praise, and rent a motorbike to ride around the old town.

cons: Cheapest rooms are small and basic, thin walls, some fan-only

entries.storyHtml: If you want a clean, high-scoring room with no guesswork, HOP INN Lopburi is it — scoring 8.6 from 300 reviews, the highest in this guide. It's a budget chain whose selling point is clean, dependable rooms at one flat rate you can book without second-guessing, on the Asia Highway (Phahonyothin) in Tha Sala near Big C, making in-and-out by car very easy. Real guest reviews praise the clean, tidy rooms, comfy beds, plenty of free parking, and price certainty with no haggling. The trade-offs: no pool, no restaurant, no breakfast, and roadside rooms catch some traffic noise. Best for travellers passing through Lopburi who just want a clean, comfortable room at a predictable price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room away from the main road or on a higher floor for less highway noise. No breakfast, but Big C and restaurants are nearby for a quick morning bite. It's about a 10-minute drive into the old town to see the monkeys and temples.

entries.storyHtml: The old-town budget pick with the most data behind it — Windsor Resort Lopburi has the most reviews in this guide at 870, scoring 8.0 from ฿580. It's an in-town resort in a quirky European/Dutch-themed building in the Pa Tan area, walking distance to Lopburi train station and near King Narai's Palace, so it's great value for train arrivals exploring the monkey town without a car. Real guest reviews praise the roomy, clean rooms, free bikes for exploring the old town, free parking, and good value. The trade-offs: no pool, rooms aren't sleek-modern, some catch train noise, and breakfast is fairly basic. Best for anyone who wants an affordable old-town base within walking distance of the train station.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Resort Zone room set further back for more quiet and less train noise. Borrow the free bikes to ride out to Phra Prang Sam Yot and see the monkeys in the old town. Arriving by train is the best value — you can walk over from Lopburi station.
pros: Most reviews in this guide 870 · solid data, from ฿580
Walk to train station, near Narai's Palace and old town
Quirky European-themed building · roomy, clean rooms (from reviews)
Free bikes · free parking · good value

entries.name: The Charlotte Smart Hotel Lopburi

entries.mrtTag: 📍 New town Lopburi · Soi Tha Sala 3 · near Big C
entries.addr: Soi Tha Sala 3, Tha Sala, Mueang Lopburi
entries.storyHtml: For a new, clean room with breakfast on a budget, The Charlotte Smart Hotel Lopburi is the freshest building in this guide — opened around 2021 — scoring 8.4 from 120 reviews from ฿700. It sits in the new town around Tha Sala–Khao Sam Yot, near Big C and the Narai roundabout. Real guest reviews praise the clean, new rooms, many with mountain-view balconies, free breakfast, and free private parking, which makes it good value for a new build at this price. The trade-offs: no pool, breakfast is basic, and it's a fair drive from the old town so you'll want a car. Best for self-drivers who want a new, clean, comfortable room in town at a budget-friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Deluxe Room with Balcony for the mountain-view balcony — the highlight of this new build. Have the free breakfast before heading out. It's about a 10-minute drive to the old town for the monkeys and temples; have a ride-hailing app ready if you don't have a car.

entries.storyHtml: A good-value in-town hotel whose selling point is roomy rooms with balconies at a budget price — JRD Grand Place Hotel scores 8.3 from 40 reviews from ฿660. It's in the Pa Tan area of new-town Lopburi near the centre, more convenient to get around than many of the Tha Sala options. Real guest reviews praise the spacious rooms, balconies in many of them, friendly service, an on-site restaurant, and free private parking. The trade-offs: no pool, a limited breakfast spread, some decor showing its age, and a still-modest review base (40) worth reading around. Best for self-drivers visiting Lopburi or here on business who want a comfortable, budget room in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room with a balcony when booking — they feel roomier and brighter. There's an on-site restaurant but a limited breakfast spread; town restaurants are close if you want variety. Review numbers are still modest, so read across multiple sources before booking.

entries.storyHtml: A few-hundred-baht stay that throws in breakfast and roomy rooms — Benjatara Boutique Place Resort is a good-value in-town resort scoring 7.9 from 201 reviews from ฿520 (breakfast included). It's in the new town around Khao Sam Yot on Soi Tha Sala, near Big C and about a 10-minute drive from Phra Prang Sam Yot. Real guest reviews praise the spacious, clean rooms, cold A/C, the quiet setting, family rooms with two king beds, and convenient parking. The trade-offs: no pool, simple rooms and decor for the price, a limited breakfast selection, and Wi-Fi that's occasionally patchy. Best for self-drivers who want a comfortable room in town at a budget price that includes breakfast.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a group or family, ask for the Family Room with two king beds (~32 sqm) — roomier and better value. Open your map app before arriving, as you turn off the main road into a soi. If you need to work online, bring a mobile-data backup.

entries.storyHtml: A light-priced roadside stay that's easy to find and drive to — Phetlada Pavilion & Resort is a roadside boutique resort scoring 7.9 from 207 reviews from just ฿450. It's on Phahonyothin Rd around Khao Sam Yot, near a 7-Eleven and a gas station, very easy in and out for self-drivers. Real guest reviews praise the roomy rooms, free parking, and the convenience of the roadside location. The trade-offs to be clear about: the building is showing its age, cleanliness isn't consistent across every room, and details on breakfast/pool should be confirmed before booking. Best for travellers passing through Lopburi or wanting an easy roadside stay on the Asia Highway at a light price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's an easy-to-find roadside resort, handy for an overnight on a long drive. Cleanliness varies room to room, so if you walk in, ask to see the room first. Confirm breakfast and pool details when booking.

entries.storyHtml: Closing the list is a good-value in-town hotel with roomy, quiet rooms at a budget price — Grand Lopburi scores 7.9 from 180 reviews from ฿650. It's in the new town around Tha Sala, about 1.6 km from the centre, near Big C and the Narai roundabout. Real guest reviews praise the spacious ~30 sqm rooms, soft beds, cold A/C, the quiet (it sits back from the main road), and VIP/Studio rooms with balconies and a small kitchenette. The trade-offs: no pool, no breakfast, the entrance is a slightly tricky turn off the main road, and some decor is simple for the price. Best for self-drivers who want a comfortable, roomy room in town at a budget price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a balcony, ask for a VIP/Studio room when booking — they're roomier with a sitting area. Open your map app before arriving, as you turn into a soi about 200 m off the main road. No breakfast, but Big C and new-town restaurants are close for a morning bite.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms and can change by date and season — always check live prices and compare 3 sites before booking · this guide hand-picks only the genuinely good-value budget stays scoring 7.9+ — we left out the 4-star hotel, the Pa Sak dam-area stays, and anything below the score threshold, to keep it to stays that are real value for money, which is why it's an honest 8 rather than a padded 10 · these are budget 2–3 star stays, so they come with trade-offs for the price: some have fan rooms, most have no pool, and new-town stays are a ~10-minute drive from the monkeys in the old town, so read each stay's notes before booking · all 8 are bookable across Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com, so you can compare every site · during the King Narai Festival and the sunflower-bloom season (roughly November–January), stays fill fast, so book ahead · Lopburi has no metro; the old town is walkable, while a rental car or self-driving is easiest elsewhere · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about budget Lopburi hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which budget Lopburi stay is the best value?
faq.a: By value (score-to-price plus saved transport), Noom Guesthouse from ฿350 scoring 8.2 is the best value here — it's the cheapest and lets you walk to the monkeys, temples, and train station without a car · if you want the highest score and guaranteed clean rooms, HOP INN Lopburi ฿650 scoring 8.6 is the safest pick · and the old-town budget option with the most data behind it is Windsor Resort ฿580 (870 reviews)

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget Lopburi hotels cost?
faq.a: In this guide, roughly ฿350–700 a night · the cheapest end is Noom Guesthouse from ฿350 (fan room), Phetlada ฿450, Benjatara ฿520, and Windsor ฿580 · slightly higher are HOP INN and Grand Lopburi at ฿650, JRD at ฿660, and The Charlotte Smart Hotel at ฿700 · all are approximate starting rates outside peak season; during the King Narai Festival and the sunflower-bloom season prices rise and rooms fill fast

faq.q: ❓ Visiting Lopburi without a car by train — where should I stay?
faq.a: Pick an old-town stay within walking distance of the sights · Noom Guesthouse ฿350, the cheapest here, a wooden house walkable to the train station, Phra Prang Sam Yot, and the monkeys · Windsor Resort ฿580, a resort walkable to the station, near Narai's Palace, with free bikes and the most reviews at 870 · both are in the old town where you can reach the key sights on foot without a car

faq.q: ❓ Self-driving and want a roomy room with parking — which area?
faq.a: Choose a new-town stay (Tha Sala–Khao Sam Yot) with roomy rooms and free parking · The Charlotte Smart Hotel ฿700, a new build with free breakfast · JRD Grand Place ฿660, roomy rooms with balconies · Grand Lopburi ฿650, roomy and quiet · HOP INN ฿650, clean rooms on the Asia Highway · Benjatara ฿520, roomy rooms with breakfast · this zone is a ~10-minute drive into the old town for the monkeys

faq.q: ❓ Which budget Lopburi stays include breakfast?
faq.a: Two here do · Benjatara Boutique Place Resort ฿520, roomy rooms with breakfast included and free parking, and The Charlotte Smart Hotel ฿700, a new build with free breakfast and many rooms with mountain-view balconies · the more budget picks like Noom, HOP INN, and Grand Lopburi mostly don't include breakfast, but restaurants and Big C are close for a morning bite

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Lopburi hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion period, so always open all 3 and compare before booking — all 8 stays in this guide are bookable across all 3 sites, and every review page has price-comparison links, which can save tens to hundreds of baht a night, especially during the King Narai Festival and the sunflower-bloom season when rooms fill fast
